findings.finding: Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂. Cyclic K‑N‑K'‑B forces ∠KBN=∠K'BN ⇒ K lies on Apollonius circle of B wrt EF, giving relation between BK and BN. Using power of B w.r.t. (BKT) and (BKN) yields CT·NB/(BT·NE)= (BC·BN)/(BN·NE)=BC/NE. Max occurs when NE minimal; from incircle geometry NE = s−a = (AB+AC−BC)/2. With BC fixed, minimize AB+AC → isosceles AB=AC (but AB≠AC, approach limit). Hence α = lim_{n→∞} BC/( (2·BC−BC)/2 ) = 2. So p=2, q=0 → floor(2^{0^2})=1 mod 99991.

Insights: BD,CD are Fibonacci → BC=Fₙ₊₂, s‑b=Fₙ, s‑c=Fₙ₊₁. Use coordinates B(0,0),C(a,0),D(Fₙ,0),I(Fₙ,r). Express F,E as projections of I onto AB,AC. K = second intersection of (A,F,E) with circumcircle Ω. K′ is reflection across EF; N is foot from D to EF. Circle through B,K tangent to BN meets BC at T. Compute ratio R=(CT·NB)/(BT·NE). Impose cyclic condition KNK′B ⇒ a relation between angles → algebraic equation linking side lengths (or r). Maximize R over admissible triangles for each n; as n→∞ (even n) R approaches a constant α = p+√q. Finally compute ⌊p^{q^p}⌋ mod 99991. Pitfalls: handling reflection K′, cyclic condition, and maximizing R (use calculus or boundary cases).

Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂, b−c=Fₙ₋₁.  For each n solve geometry (incircle, AFE‑Ω intersection K, K′, N) and enforce B,K,N,K′ cyclic → one/two feasible c.
